measured_zone_distribution.note: Lap-average method. Retained for provenance only. Use true_zone_distribution instead — it is computed per-second from raw FIT and is definitive.

z4_drought.what_was_claimed: 61 days with no Z4; 32 consecutive rides at zero; Aug and Sep 2026 both 0.0% Z4.
z4_drought.why_it_was_wrong: Derived from lap-average binning. Classifying a 10-minute lap by its mean HR erases Z4 minutes inside it. Per-second data shows Z4 in EVERY month of the dataset.
z4_drought.truth: Z4 never absent. Aug 2026: 28.5 min (season low). Sep 2026: 73.1 min (recovering). Last Z4 ride: 2026-09-24 (11.9 min Z4). Source: training.db per-second analysis.

structured_z4_precedent.finding: Ettore already has a proven structured-Z4 habit — it was indoor. 4 winter trainer sessions contained repeated Z4 intervals (28-35 Z4 laps each, laps averaging 2.8 min). Outdoor rides never reproduced this: outdoor laps average 10.6 min and only ever contain 1-2 Z4 laps.
structured_z4_precedent.interpretation: The capability is not missing and does not need building from zero — it needs re-activating. The winter indoor block is the template.

true_zone_distribution.method: Per-second from raw FIT files via training.db ETL. Every sample classified by instantaneous HR, weighted by actual sample interval. No binning, no Garmin summaries.

z5_reality.correction: Previously reported as 0.0%. That was a lap-averaging artifact. Z5 is small but real: 12.5 min across 9 rides, peak 193bpm.

weekday_power_meter.finding: The weekday bike DID have a power meter. 22 flat rides carry power data from Sep 2025 to 27 May 2026. Every flat ride from 1 Jun 2026 onward has none.
weekday_power_meter.implication: Power on the weekday bike stopped ~end of May 2026 (battery, pairing, or the meter was moved). If it can be revived, the Tue/Thu interval sessions could be run on watts instead of RPE+HR — a material upgrade to plan precision.

ftp_reassessment.verdict: FTP 256W is not supported by any power data in 13 months. It was a manual Garmin entry, never tested. Evidence converges on ~235W.
ftp_reassessment.method: Per-second analysis of the Tre Valli Varesine ride (19 Sep 2026) — the only near-maximal sustained effort in the dataset.

tre_valli_evidence.hr_during: rose to 180bpm, which is 99% of the 2026 season max of 181bpm
tre_valli_evidence.final_5min_of_effort: HR 178bpm at 249W — he was at the limit
tre_valli_evidence.why_20min_is_misleading: The climb lasted ~15-16 min. The PDC drops 19W between 18min (257W) and 20min (238W) — a physiological curve cannot fall that fast. The 20-min window is forced to include post-climb descent, so it measures terrain, not threshold.

estimates.note: W'=8141J, still low — suggests even this was sub-maximal at short durations

ftp_reassessment.why_it_matters: Zone boundaries scale with FTP. At 256W, power Z4 starts at 231W — above his actual threshold — so Z4 was close to unreachable and looked like a training deficit. At 235W, Z4 starts at 212W and measured Z4+ time rises from 6.3% to 12.1%, close to the 15% target. The deficit was largely an artifact of a wrong FTP.
ftp_reassessment.action: FTP now set to 245W (manual entry Sep 24 2026). Use this for all interval targets.
ftp_reassessment.primary_basis: 15-minute maximal climb effort on Tre Valli Varesine, 19 Sep 2026

fifteen_min_derivation.last_3min: HR 178bpm at 244W — he was at the ceiling
fifteen_min_derivation.was_maximal: Yes. HR reached 99% of season max and stayed there. Treat as a true 15-min max.

at_256w.15min_261w: 102% of FTP — implausibly low for a maximal 15min ✗

cross_validation.conclusion: Three independent durations all fit 235W and all contradict 256W.

power_zones_corrected.current_ftp_note: Manually set Sep 25 2026, matching evidence-based estimate from Sep 19 15-min climb (261W × 0.90)

true_pdc.method: Mean maximal power computed from per-second power records in training.db. No Garmin summaries.
true_pdc.corrections: 60-min best is 216W, not the 163W previously recorded. 30-min (226W) and all sub-5min durations were never computed before.
true_pdc.data_quality_note: 1s peaks above ~1200W (2335W on 3 Aug, 1541W on 4 Jul, 1254W on 9 Aug) are sensor spikes, not real. Flagged, excluded from interpretation.

self_detected_efforts.method: Efforts found by scanning the per-second signal for contiguous runs above a threshold (short dips tolerated). Garmin lap boundaries are not used at all.
self_detected_efforts.insight: 221 discrete sustained Z4 HR efforts across 86 of 184 rides (47%). The longest is 35m36s on 18 Apr 2026. This is not a rider who lacks threshold exposure.

climbs_detected.method: Climbs detected from smoothed altitude gradient alone — sustained positive-gradient segments with >=30m gain and >=120s duration. Garmin laps not used.

decoupling.method: Power:HR efficiency ratio, first vs second half of MOVING time only (speed>1m/s), per-second. Stopped time excluded so cafe stops cannot fake drift.
